messages:
sara-sales: Quick sync  NimbusHealth wants a Private deployment POC next week. Main asks from their infra/security: 1) they require stable outbound IPs for allowlisting, 2) they need confirmation on whether PrivateLink or VPC peering is recommended, and 3) pricing delta for dedicated static EIPs vs standard shared egress. Can we triage? cc @matt-netops @devon-arch @emily-security

matt-netops: For stable outbound IPs we have two patterns: (A) BYOIP / customer-provided NAT IPs routed from their edge into the Private deploy; or (B) Redwood allocates static EIPs in the customer's account and we SNAT there. Pattern B requires us to run a managed NAT/proxy in their VPC or route via TGW. Both are doable for POC but B adds setup time.

devon-arch: Regarding PrivateLink vs peering: if customer security wants strict control and minimal cross-account routing, PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is cleaner: it terminates in their account and avoids route table exposure. Peering/TGW gives more control for large CIDR ranges and is cheaper at scale. For a POC with tight allowlist needs, PrivateLink + explicit egress IPs is the lowest-friction for auditors.

emily-security: A couple constraints from Nimbuss questionnaire: they require (a) proof that egress IPs will not change during the POC window, (b) audit log access for connection establishment, and (c) an escalation contact for network issues. Also they want to avoid TLS MITM; TLS-inspect will be enabled on their perimeter. Any notes on SNI cert exposure?

jen-engineer: If TLS inspection is on their side: ensure they whitelist our hostnames (api.redwood.inference, ingest.redwood.inference) or allow SNI passthrough. If they force cert re-signing, we need a security review. For IP stability we can offer a 72-hour freeze window for the prefix used in the POC (we'll document the SLA in the runbook).

matt-netops: Practical firewall snippet I hand to customers (short):
```
# Nimbus outbound allowlist (example)
allow tcp 443 to api.redwood.inference   # FQDN-based allow recommended
allow tcp 443 to 18.197.45.0/28        # reserved egress block for this POC (if IP-based allowlist)
allow tcp 443 to vpce-abcde123.vpce-svc  # if using AWS PrivateLink (allow VPCE hostname or managed IPs)
```
Note: VPCE managed IPs can shift; recommend hostname unless policy forbids DNS-based rules.

sara-sales: Good. What about the pricing ask? Nimbus is budget-conscious; they prefer to avoid per-connector monthly fees if possible.

finance-bot: Pricing summary (draft): shared egress (hosted routing) = no connector surcharge; dedicated static EIPs per connector = $1,500 one-time setup + $300/month per connector for reserved NAT/proxy capacity and monitoring. Enterprise discounts may apply for annual commit. Confirm with finance for final quote.

devon-arch: Ops note: if they choose PrivateLink + customer-provided egress IPs we can avoid the monthly connector surcharge because traffic exits via their NAT. If they want Redwood-managed static EIPs (we attach EIPs in their account), surcharge applies. For POC timeline choose customer BYOIP if they can provide it quickly.

emily-security: For the security questionnaire: we can provide network diagrams showing PrivateLink flow, signed runbook for cutover/backout, and a scoped SOC/PCI data-flow statement (POC-level). I'll prepare a redacted audit log sample showing connection timestamps.

jen-engineer: Canary strategy: start with 5% traffic to Redwood backend, validate success for 1 hour, then increase to 25% before full ramp. If outbound failures spike >5% for 3 consecutive minutes, automatic rollback to previous route. We'll need Nimbus to configure their LB/ingress to support weighted routing or header-based routing for canary.

sara-sales: Nimbus also asked who's the on-call for network troubleshooting during the POC window (they want a phone escalation). Can someone volunteer?

matt-netops: I'll take primary on-call for the POC window. Provide my cell and I'll add to the escalation list. Also add the ops-runbook entry: run tcpdump on NAT instance and check ALB logs in their account if using PrivateLink.

devon-arch: Deliverables timeline: (1) allowlist CSV (IPs + FQDNs) + runbook by Wednesday EOD, (2) pricing confirmation for static EIP path by Thursday noon, (3) security artifacts (diagram + audit sample) by Thursday EOD. I'll own 1 and 2; @emily-security owns 3.

sara-sales: Nimbus wants the final artifact set by Friday to approve. I9ll set the kickoff for Monday. Devon/Emily/Matt please drop the artifacts in this thread as you have them. Thanks! :rocket:
